newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Club agrees Niger debt restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club agrees Niger debt restructuring.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor nations said on Monday it had agreed to restructure Niger's foreign debt, giving it the most generous terms of debt relief currently available to poor nations.
It said in a statement it had agreed to give Niger "Naples terms" of debt relief, reducing payments due between 1996 and 199 by up to 67 percent. The agreement was made at a meeting last week.
Creditor countries agreed to meet again under certain conditions to consider, by mid-1999, Niger's stock of debt.
They could also make debt for nature, debt for aid, debt for equity or other local currency swaps up to 20 percent of the debts concerned, the Paris Club said.
The debt relief decision follows an agreement between Niger and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on an economic reform programme, approved by the IMF in June this year.
The debt relief is on payments due under the period covered by the IMF agreement, which runs to mid-1999.
